sentences.en: In the early 1990s, Jim Heckman traveled to Corpus Christi, Texas.
sentences.zh: 20世纪90年代初，吉姆·赫克曼前往得克萨斯州科珀斯克里斯蒂。

sentences.en: He was there to see something that had been described to him as a miracle.
sentences.zh: 他去那里是为了看一样被向他描述为奇迹的东西。

sentences.en: It was a program for students who had dropped out of high school.
sentences.zh: 这是一个针对高中辍学生的项目。

sentences.en: And they said, you know, we have a program which will take high school dropouts,
sentences.zh: 他们说，你知道的，我们有一个项目可以收留高中辍学生，

sentences.en: people who had dropped out in ninth grade, or before actually,
sentences.zh: 那些在九年级或更早其实就辍学的人，

sentences.en: and converted them into high school graduates within two to three months in our program.
sentences.zh: 并在我们项目中两到三个月内把他们转变成高中毕业生。

sentences.en: And then we send them out to the workplace.
sentences.zh: 然后我们把他们送进职场。

sentences.en: So I said, well, this is amazing.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，好吧，这太惊人了。

sentences.en: The program that gave young people a second chance is now known widely across the country.
sentences.zh: 这个给年轻人第二次机会的项目现在在全国广为人知。
它被称为普通同等学历证书（GED）。

sentences.en: Which was a program which students studied for a teSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个学生为考试而学习的项目。

sentences.en: And at the end of the test, they were certified as legitimate high school graduates.
sentences.zh: 在考试结束时，他们被认证为合格的高中毕业生。

sentences.en: There were plenty of individual success stories.
sentences.zh: 有很多个人的成功故事。

sentences.en: But Jim is an economist, and he wanted to know whether, on average,
sentences.zh: 但吉姆是一位经济学家，他想知道，平均而言，

sentences.en: people with a GED were as successful as those with a high school diploma.
sentences.zh: 拥有GED的人是否和拥有高中毕业证书的人一样成功。

sentences.en: He started by looking at their test scores.
sentences.zh: 他从查看他们的考试成绩开始。

sentences.en: What really surprised me was their test scores were virtually the same.
sentences.zh: 真正让我惊讶的是，他们的考试成绩实际上是一样的。

sentences.en: Within a few months, the GED program was allowing students to catch up with peers
sentences.zh: 在几个月内，GED项目让学生能够赶上同龄人，

sentences.en: who had spent years in high school.
sentences.zh: 那些在高中度过了多年的人。
但随后吉姆进行了更深入的调查。

sentences.en: Were GED grads holding on to jobs and long-term relationships, staying out of trouble?
sentences.zh: 获得GED的人能否保住工作和长期的关系，远离麻烦？

sentences.en: If you looked at the GEDs, you realized they weren't doing so well.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看获得GED的人，你会意识到他们过得并不好。

sentences.en: They were likely, it turned out, if they got a job, to quit the job or be fired.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，如果他们找到工作，他们很可能会辞职或被解雇。

sentences.en: If they went into marriage or some partnership, how stable were those compared to the ordinary
sentences.zh: 如果他们进入婚姻或某种伴侣关系，与普通高中毕业生相比，

sentences.en: Much more likely to commit crime.
Why were GED recipients struggling if they had the same test scores as high school graduates?
sentences.zh: 为什么获得GED的人如果和高中毕业生有相同的考试成绩却在苦苦挣扎？

sentences.en: It was kind of a revealing insight that these people were as smart as high school graduates,
sentences.zh: 这算是一种具有启示性的洞察，这些人其实和高中毕业生一样聪明，

sentences.en: measured by the kind of test that so much public policy focuses on.
sentences.zh: 通过大量公共政策所关注的那种测试来衡量。

sentences.en: But in real life, they were really not succeeding in any real way.
sentences.zh: 但在现实生活中，他们在任何真正的意义上都没有成功。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, untangling the mystery Jim Heckman discovered in Corpus Christi
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的脑回路》，我们将解开吉姆·赫克曼在科珀斯克里斯蒂发现的谜团，

sentences.en: and the astounding implications his findings have for public policy.
sentences.zh: 以及他的发现在公共政策方面产生的惊人影响。

sentences.en: James Heckman is a professor at the University of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·赫克曼是芝加哥大学的教授。

sentences.en: In 2000, he won the Nobel Prize in Economics.
Some of his early work focused on programs like the GED that are designed to give young
sentences.zh: 他早期的一些工作集中在像GED这样旨在给年轻人第二次机会的项目上。

sentences.en: Jim found that these programs were succeeding in getting young people to do well in tests,
sentences.zh: 吉姆发现这些项目在让年轻人考好试方面取得了成功，

sentences.en: but failing when it came to improving their outcomes in life.
sentences.zh: 但在改善他们的人生结果方面却失败了。

sentences.en: It prompted him to ask broader questions about the American educational system.
sentences.zh: 这促使他对美国教育体系提出了更广泛的问题。

sentences.en: I realized that the whole educational establishment, at least the establishment that looked at test
sentences.zh: 我意识到整个教育体制，至少是那个看重考试成绩、

sentences.en: scores and that valued schools and valued people by these test scores, really was just
sentences.zh: 重视学校并通过这些考试成绩来评价人的体制，确实只是

sentences.en: missing important dimensions of human behavior.
sentences.zh: 忽略了人类行为的重要维度。

sentences.en: And so that brought me onto a subject which has fascinated me and which I think is really
sentences.zh: 所以这把我带入了一个让我着迷的主题，我认为这对于成功以及理解成功和失败

sentences.en: important for success and understanding success and failure.
And that is the notion of what I call non-cognitive skills.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所说的非认知技能的概念。

sentences.en: By non-cognitive skills, I meant skills that weren't measured by these tests.
sentences.zh: 通过非认知技能，我指的是那些无法通过这些测试来衡量的技能。

sentences.en: And what I found, and that surprised me, was that those non-cognitive skills were extremely
sentences.zh: 而我所发现的、令我惊讶的是，那些非认知技能极其

sentences.en: And then when you think about it, you say, well, what an idiot.
sentences.zh: 然后当你仔细想想，你会说，真是个白痴。

sentences.en: You know, and then you go back to everything you ever heard from the time you were a child.
sentences.zh: 你知道，然后你回想起你从小到大听过的一切。

sentences.en: The Aesop's fables, the tortoise and the hare, and, you know, Teddy Roosevelt saying, you know,
sentences.zh: 伊索寓言，龟兔赛跑，你知道的，西奥多·罗斯福说，

sentences.en: it's the man of grit and the person who would go down, who gets back up again and tries.
sentences.zh: 拥有坚韧不拔精神的人，那个倒下、再次站起来并尝试的人。

sentences.en: And, you know, all of the mottos we quote to our children and that many presidents and leaders
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，所有我们对孩子们说的座右铭，以及许多总统和领导人
几个世纪以来对我们说的话。

sentences.en: I mean, it's in many religious teachings.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它存在于许多宗教教义中。

sentences.en: So I said, you know, this is obviously true.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，你知道，这显然是真的。

sentences.en: But it turned out that in psychology at that time, there was a sense that somehow personality
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，那时的心理学界认为，某种程度上，人格

sentences.en: and the subject of personality was kind of, you know, a dark and unrigorous corner.
sentences.zh: 和人格这个主题有点像是一个黑暗且不够严谨的角落。

sentences.en: Whereas the IQ test, there we actually had machinery to measure it.
sentences.zh: 而智商测试，我们实际上有测量它的机制。

sentences.en: We had ways to score tests and so forth and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们有给测试评分的方法，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So what I did then is that started a lifetime investigation on the social and emotional skills.
sentences.zh: 所以我所做的就是开启了一项关于社会和情感技能的终身调查。

sentences.en: And there's evidence, by the way, that staying in school, that working through, will build those skills.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，有证据表明，留在学校里、坚持不懈，将建立这些技能。

sentences.en: In 2014, the makers of the GED overhauled the exam, partly in response to the work of Jim Heckman
sentences.zh: 2014年，GED的制定者彻底修改了考试，部分是为了响应吉姆·赫克曼
和其他研究人员的工作。

sentences.en: A spokesman for the GED program says the new test more effectively measures problem-solving skills,
sentences.zh: GED项目的一位发言人表示，新测试更有效地衡量了解决问题的能力、

sentences.en: It also demands more from test takers by way of preparation and grit.
sentences.zh: 它还在准备和坚韧方面对考生提出了更多要求。

sentences.en: To put it another way, the GED now does more to tap into non-cognitive skills.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，GED现在在挖掘非认知技能方面做得更多。

sentences.en: Jim says these kinds of skills can be summed up with a single word, character.
sentences.zh: 吉姆说，这些技能可以用一个词来概括：品格。

sentences.en: One time in American education, I mean, I'm talking a long time ago,
sentences.zh: 在美国教育的某个时期，我的意思是，我说的是很久以前，

sentences.en: when Horace Mann was devising the first common schools for all Americans,
sentences.zh: 当贺拉斯·曼为所有美国人设计第一批公立学校时，

sentences.en: character training was literally part of the curriculum.
sentences.zh: 品格训练实际上就是课程的一部分。

sentences.en: I think Horace Mann has a quote in the 1840s when he was setting up this movement.
sentences.zh: 我想贺拉斯·曼在1940年代建立这个运动时有一句名言。

sentences.en: And basically, he said something which says it all, really, you know,
sentences.zh: 基本上，他说了一句真正能说明一切的话，你知道的，

sentences.en: that reading, writing, and arithmetic is but a small portion of what we teach in school.
sentences.zh: 阅读、写作和算术只是我们在学校教授的一小部分。

sentences.en: And then he goes on to say that what we're really teaching is character.
sentences.zh: 然后他接着说，我们真正教的是品格。

sentences.en: We're teaching children how to stay on task, to control their emotions, to work with others,
sentences.zh: 我们教孩子们如何专心致志、控制情绪、与他人合作、

sentences.en: And so this whole bundle of attributes we know are important in life,
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道这整套属性在生活中很重要，

sentences.en: and the common school was designed basically to foster all of those.
sentences.zh: 而公立学校的设计基本上就是为了培养所有这些。

sentences.en: A clear example of character education was the hugely popular textbook series called McGuffey Readers.
sentences.zh: 品格教育的一个清晰例子是极其受欢迎的名为《麦克加菲读本》的教科书系列。

sentences.en: You'd find them in many classrooms between the mid-19th century and the mid-20th century.
sentences.zh: 你会在19世纪中期到20世纪中期之间的许多教室里找到它们。

sentences.en: The textbooks were filled with stories about how to live a virtuous life.
sentences.zh: 这些教科书里充满了关于如何过上有美德的生活的故事。

sentences.en: This one is about a hen who works hard to take care of her 12 chicks.
sentences.zh: 这个故事讲的是一只母鸡努力照顾她12只小鸡的故事。

sentences.en: She asks them to follow her as she jumps across a brook to a stone, but they don't obey.
sentences.zh: 她让他们跟着她跳过一条小溪到一块石头上，但他们不听话。

sentences.en: Oh, mother, we can't, we can't, we can't, said all the little chickens.
sentences.zh: 哦，妈妈，我们不能，我们不能，我们不能，所有的小鸡都说。

sentences.en: Yes, you can, if you try, said the old hen.
sentences.zh: 是的，只要你努力，你就能，老母鸡说。

sentences.en: Just flap your wings, as I did, and you can jump over.
sentences.zh: 只要像我一样扇动翅膀，你就能跳过去。

sentences.en: Only one of the chickens, Chippy, even tries.
sentences.zh: 只有一只小鸡，奇皮，甚至尝试了。

sentences.en: When they got home, the old hen began to look about for something to eat.
sentences.zh: 当他们到家时，老母鸡开始四处寻找吃的东西。

sentences.en: She soon found, near the back door, a piece of bread.
sentences.zh: 她很快在后门附近发现了一块面包。

sentences.en: So she called the chickens, and they all ran up to her, each one trying to get a bite at the piece of bread.
sentences.zh: 于是她召唤小鸡们，它们都跑向她，每一个都试图去咬一口面包。

sentences.en: No, no, said the old hen, this bread is for Chippy.
sentences.zh: 不，不，老母鸡说，这块面包是给奇皮的。

sentences.en: He is the only one of my children that really tried to jump to the stone.
sentences.zh: 他是我的孩子中唯一一个真正努力跳到石头上的人。

sentences.en: One of the most interesting is a story about a couple of boys who ran away from school, played hooky, stole a boat,
sentences.zh: 最有趣的故事之一是关于几个男孩逃学、旷课、偷了一条船，

sentences.en: and then the ocean came up, and they were nearly drowned.
sentences.zh: 然后海潮上涨，他们差点淹死。

sentences.en: And finally, by the grace of God, they were thrown onto the beach and saved.
sentences.zh: 最后，靠着上帝的恩典，他们被冲上沙滩并得救了。

sentences.en: And they learned their lesson, and they never ran away from school again, and they did their lessons.
sentences.zh: 他们吸取了教训，再也没有逃学，并且完成了功课。

sentences.en: So there were a lot of stories like that.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多像这样的故事。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, from the standpoint of some elements of society, and I really mean it was unfortunate,
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，从社会某些阶层的角度来看，我真的是指这很不幸，

sentences.en: those early lessons were more or less using the Bible, the Protestant Bible, as the touchstone to teach morality and character.
sentences.zh: 那些早期的课程多多少少是以圣经、新教圣经为基准来教导道德和品格的。

sentences.en: And then, of course, other groups as they came to the United States, more Catholics, for example, Jews, another group.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，当其他群体来到美国时，例如更多的天主教徒、犹太人，另一个群体。

sentences.en: As they came, they found this very offensive.
sentences.zh: 当他们来的时候，他们发现这非常具有冒犯性。

sentences.en: They didn't want to get their children indoctrinated.
sentences.zh: 他们不想让自己的孩子被灌输思想。

sentences.en: And so that aspect of character gradually got edited out of the common school.
sentences.zh: 所以品格的那一方面逐渐从公立学校中被删除了。

sentences.en: And then psychology, meanwhile, had this, quote, development, this great breakthrough that was really cognitive psychology,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，心理学有了所谓的“发展”，这一伟大的突破实际上是认知心理学，

sentences.en: that really said IQ and cognition and pure problem-solving ability.
sentences.zh: 它确实声称智商、认知和纯粹的解决问题能力。

sentences.en: That was really the be-all and end-all of an education, and that we shouldn't worry about this touchy-feely stuff,
sentences.zh: 这才是教育的全部意义所在，我们不应该担心这些感伤的东西，

sentences.en: building Americans, learning to work with others, understanding democracy.
sentences.zh: 培养美国人，学习与他人合作，理解民主。

sentences.en: All of that was viewed as junk.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都被视为垃圾。

sentences.en: And it really hit the trash can in the late 50s when Sputnik surprised Americans.
sentences.zh: 在50年代末，当斯普特尼克号让美国人感到震惊时，它真的遭到了唾弃。

sentences.en: And literally, if you read the education journals of the time, what really was needed was, you know,
sentences.zh: 老实说，如果你阅读当时的教育期刊，真正需要的是，你知道的，

sentences.en: get your math right, get your science right, and the rest of it was kind of taken for granted.
sentences.zh: 搞好你的数学，搞好你的科学，其余的基本上都是理所当然的。

sentences.en: So this is fascinating because what you're pointing out is that for a long time,
sentences.zh: 所以这很迷人，因为你指出的是，很长一段时间以来，

sentences.en: the link between character and what was taught in school had a religious component to it.
sentences.zh: 品格与学校教授的内容之间的联系具有宗教成分。

sentences.en: And as the country became perhaps more secular or more diverse,
sentences.zh: 随着国家变得或许更加世俗化或更加多元化，

sentences.en: people had some resistance to bringing those religious ideas along.
sentences.zh: 人们对引入这些宗教思想产生了一些抵触。

sentences.en: But, of course, you don't need religion to teach questions related to character.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，你不需要宗教来教导与品格相关的问题。

sentences.en: Modern psychology has done a lot of thinking about some of these traits.
sentences.zh: 现代心理学对其中一些特质进行了很多思考。

sentences.en: What traits are we talking about when we use the term character?
sentences.zh: 当我们使用“品格”这个词时，我们究竟在谈论什么特质？

sentences.en: What kind of traits are these?
Well, there's a range of traits.
What I mean is the ability to plan.
How well can I actually plan my life forward?
sentences.zh: 我实际上能把我的生活向前规划得有多好？

sentences.en: How well can I persist on a task?
sentences.zh: 我在一项任务上能坚持多久？

sentences.en: If I experience failure, how far can I go and bounce back and try, try again?
sentences.zh: 如果我经历失败，我能走多远并振作起来，再接再厉？

sentences.en: How open am I to experience?
sentences.zh: 我对经验的开放程度如何？

sentences.en: So, in other words, am I closed off?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我是封闭的吗？

sentences.en: Do I kind of shun contact with new ideas and with new people?
sentences.zh: 我是否有点回避与新思想和新人的接触？

sentences.en: How agreeable am I in the sense of, you know, I may find somebody disagrees with me,
sentences.zh: 我的随和度如何，在这个意义上，你知道，我可能会发现有人不同意我的观点，

sentences.en: but that doesn't mean I have to fight them.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着我必须与他们争斗。

sentences.en: It means I listen, they listen to me, and we can agree, and we can also agree to disagree.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我倾听，他们倾听我，我们可以达成一致，我们也可以求同存异。

sentences.en: But there's a sense of having a sense of propriety about the relationship.
sentences.zh: 但这有一种对关系的得体感。

sentences.en: So this term character is a quite broad term, really, very elastic in some ways.
sentences.zh: 所以“品格”这个词是一个相当广泛的词，在某些方面真的很灵活。

sentences.en: One of the most important qualities that Jim identified is conscientiousness,
sentences.zh: 吉姆确定的最重要的品质之一是尽责性，

sentences.en: or what the psychologist Angela Duckworth calls grit.
sentences.zh: 或者心理学家安杰拉·达克沃思所称的坚毅。

sentences.en: Jim also found that the ability to delay gratification matters a lot.
sentences.zh: 吉姆还发现，延迟满足的能力非常重要。

sentences.en: In other words, I can see a gain.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我可以看到回报。

sentences.en: If I wait today, like, go to school, it's unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 如果我今天等待，比如去上学，这是不愉快的。

sentences.en: I don't like to teach her.
But I know that if I finish these two years, I will have much better opportunity in life.
sentences.zh: 但我知道，如果我完成这两年，我在生活中会有更好的机会。

sentences.en: So I control myself and stay in school.
sentences.zh: 所以我克制自己，坚持留在学校。

sentences.en: You know, I grin and bear it, I guess, is the way to describe it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想这就是所谓的咬牙坚持吧。

sentences.en: So I think it's this ability to manage yourself and to work with others.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一种自我管理和与他人合作的能力。

sentences.en: Do you think this is true for even Nobel Prize winners?
sentences.zh: 你觉得即便是对诺贝尔奖得主来说，这也是真的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, when you look at your own life and career, do you see sort of the role of character,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你回顾自己的人生和职业生涯时，你会发现品格、

sentences.en: of perseverance and conscientiousness and grit as in some ways being just as important
sentences.zh: 毅力、尽责精神和坚韧在某种程度上同样重要，

sentences.en: or perhaps more important than cognitive and intellectual abilities?
sentences.zh: 或者说可能比认知和智力能力更重要？

sentences.en: And the reason why I say for sure is take some truly important scientists like Marie Curie.
sentences.zh: 我之所以说当然，是因为以玛丽·居里这样真正伟大的科学家为例。

sentences.en: You know, her work, for example, in isolating radium, taking pitchblend or distilling it in the back of some sheds in Paris
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如她在巴黎某间棚屋的后头，从沥青铀矿中分离出镭、对其进行提炼的工作，

sentences.en: That was just brutal grunt work.
